Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the demo earlier - great context on how your risk ops team will use the models for transaction scoring and fraud triage. Per our call I wanted to summarize the follow-ups and ask a few clarifying questions so we can put together a targeted hosted API pricing proposal: 

Recap / asks:
- Primary workload: short-form classification + scoring on transaction payloads (prompt ~50 tokens, response ~30 tokens on average).
- Key asks: expected monthly token volume, peak TPS, and any initial budget range you have in mind.
- SLA and compliance: you mentioned SOC 2 and a standard DPA - we can include those in the enterprise addendum if needed.

Quick note on unit economics we typically use for hosted API planning: teams often target a baseline unit of $/1M tokens to compare options. If you can give a target $/1M tokens or a monthly budget range, we can show concrete pricing scenarios (committed vs on-demand, peak TPS sizing).

Next steps:
1) If you can share an estimate of expected monthly tokens and peak TPS, we'll draft 2 pricing scenarios (on-demand and 12-month committed).
2) Marissa (cc'd) will run a quick calc to show expected monthly cost and peak capacity needs so you can pass to procurement.

If it's easier, feel free to send a quick spreadsheet (volume by environment: prod/staging) - we'll use that to size dedicated throughput and to recommend batching/quantization levers.

Thanks - I'll wait on the numbers and then get a pricing sketch over by EOD tomorrow.

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the recap - that matches our notes. Quick answers below and I attached a small workbook with expected volumes by environment.

High level numbers (prod only):
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~60,000,000 tokens/month (this assumes ~200k transactions/day at ~300 tokens per transaction end-to-end).
- Peak TPS (ingest): ~25 TPS (we see bursts during reconciliation windows but 25 TPS is our expected peak sustained for ~10-15 minutes).
- Budget range: we're initially planning for $5k-$7k/month while we validate accuracy; if the economics look good we can expand committed spend.
- Target $/1M tokens for internal benchmarking: we're hoping to hit ~ $80 per 1M tokens (we're evaluating a few vendors).

We don't need advanced SLAs for the pilot, but procurement will want a ballpark for committed vs on-demand pricing for their review.

Ben / Alice - quick calc and recommendations based on Alice's numbers (see attached).

Assumptions used:
- Avg tokens per request (roundtrip): 80 tokens (50 prompt + 30 response) - matches Ben's note.
- Monthly tokens: 60M => ~750k requests/month at 80 tokens/request.
- Peak throughput: 25 TPS sustained bursts.

Pricing scenarios to consider (ballpark):
1) On-demand hosted API (no commitment)
   - If vendor list-price equivalent to $120 / 1M tokens => cost = $7,200 / month (60 * $120)
2) 12-month committed discount tier (example Redwood reserved credit)
   - At $80 / 1M tokens (your target), cost = $4,800 / month (60 * $80)
   - We could propose a hybrid: commit to 50M tokens at $70/1M and on-demand for overage at $110/1M - this lands in your $5k-$7k budget depending on exact commit.

Capacity notes:
- Peak TPS 25 is small for hosted API; we can serve that on standard shared pools with auto-scaling. For predictable latency under bursts we recommend a small dedicated capacity burst (reserved endpoints) or a provisioned TPS for critical windows (adds modest monthly cost but avoids cold-scaling delays).
- Batching & prefix caching could reduce token consumption by ~10-20% for repeatable prompts - worth experimenting in staging to bring unit cost below target.

Recommended next steps:
- Ben: share a short pricing sketch with the two scenarios (on-demand vs 12-month commit + overage).
- Alice: confirm whether procurement prefers committed proposal or pay-as-you-go for pilot.
- If procurement wants committed numbers, we'll include a draft SOW and standard DPA (attached SOW_draft.pdf).

I attached my calculation CSV for traceability.

Thanks - happy to jump on a 20-minute call to align on the commit sizing.

Marissa Cole
